references.text: The same warning that the land will vomit out its inhabitants if they do not keep God's laws and statutes. Both texts use the same image of the land vomiting out the people because of impurity.

The command to keep God's statutes and laws, with a promise of life for the one who does so. The same structure with שָׁמַר (keep) and עָשָׂה (do) in relation to חֻקֹּת (statutes) and מִשְׁפָּטִים (laws).
The continuation of the same warning, explaining that it was because of these sins that the former inhabitants were driven out of the land.
Moses urges the people of Israel to keep God's statutes and laws in order to live and take possession of the land. The same connection between obedience and inheriting the land.
A command to keep all the commands in order to live, become numerous, and enter the land. Obedience linked to the promise of the land.
An exhortation to keep all the commands in order to be strong and take possession of the land that the Lord promised to the fathers.
A warning that the Lord will uproot them from the land if they are disobedient, as fulfillment of the threat in Leviticus.
Prophetic fulfillment where Ezekiel describes how Israel was driven out of the land because of their impurity, and the land was made unclean by them.
Jeremiah mentions that the people of Israel entered the land but made it unclean with their abominations.
